Detect candidate objects in an image and build embeddings for both full-image context and object crops. Train aligned text/image embeddings with genuine positive pairs and hard negatives, taking care not to mark equivalent products as negatives. Metadata filters such as category, region, stock, and price remain explicit.

Index catalog embeddings in a sharded ANN service, retrieving a moderate shortlist before a richer visual/text reranker. Version embeddings and indexes together; support incremental additions and deletion propagation. Crop coordinates must map back to the original image for usable results. Product variants and duplicate listings need grouping so top results are not nearly identical.

Distinguish a billion indexed items from a billion queries per day; the latter averages about 11,574 QPS before peaks. Capacity planning needs both corpus size and peak query rate. Measure object localization quality, retrieval recall, product relevance, ANN recall/latency, and conversion. Use cached popular results and text/category fallbacks during index outages. This design is illustrative rather than a description of current Pinterest internals.

**Mathematical and practical explanation.** For normalized image/text embeddings, cosine similarity is their dot product, enabling a shared retrieval space. Indexing a billion items requires accounting for vector bytes, ANN overhead, replicas, and update buffers. Compress or shard only after measuring recall on real product matches, including near-duplicate variants and object crops rather than only full images. [3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.00020)

For the implementation or system context discussed above, see [1](https://medium.com/pinterest-engineering/engineering-shop-the-look-on-pinterest-45bdfa7a8d03) and [2](https://www.pinecone.io/learn/series/faiss/product-quantization/).
